records.statement: A general adult exercise program may include cardiorespiratory, resistance, flexibility, and neuromotor components; the user's primary goal determines emphasis but not dose by itself.
records.applies_to: Apparently healthy adults in the SportRX goal-first intake.
allowed_language: Your primary goal changes the weekly training emphasis.
A complete fitness plan can use more than one training mode.
disallowed_language: Selecting a goal is enough to determine your exact dose.
Every user needs the same four-part weekly plan.
records.limitations: The guidance describes population-level program components; starting dose still requires recent exposure, time, equipment, and Safety Gate constraints.

records.statement: Regular aerobic exercise can improve cardiorespiratory fitness, while frequency, intensity, time, type, volume, and progression should be matched to the person's current exposure and constraints.
records.applies_to: Apparently healthy adults receiving aerobic or general-fitness training context.
allowed_language: Aerobic training is the main component for a cardiorespiratory-fitness goal.
The starting week should reflect recent activity and available time.
disallowed_language: This exact weekly dose is optimal for everyone.
Completing the plan proves VO2max improvement.
records.limitations: General prescription principles do not replace baseline measurement or predict the magnitude of individual adaptation.

records.statement: HIIT can improve cardiorespiratory fitness in adults, but protocol heterogeneity, risk-of-bias concerns, experience, and tolerance prevent it from being a universal default.
records.applies_to: Adults for whom interval training is being considered after an appropriate Safety Gate and exposure review.
allowed_language: Intervals are one possible method for improving aerobic fitness.
Continuous aerobic work remains a valid option.
disallowed_language: HIIT is always superior.
A time-efficient protocol is automatically safe or appropriate for you.
records.limitations: The studies span different populations and protocols; SportRX must not infer individual suitability or effect size from group averages.

records.statement: Progressive resistance training improves strength and muscle size in healthy adults across many viable prescription configurations.
records.applies_to: Healthy adults undertaking progressive resistance training for at least several weeks.
allowed_language: Consistent progressive resistance training matters more than finding one perfect routine.
Several resistance-training configurations can work.
disallowed_language: Only one split or equipment type can build muscle.
This routine guarantees strength or muscle gain.
records.limitations: Evidence supports group-level adaptation and does not validate a specific SportRX pack or predict an individual's response.

records.statement: Higher loads, multiple sets, and repeated weekly exposure can enhance maximal-strength outcomes, but maximizing parameters are not automatically an appropriate starting dose.
records.applies_to: Healthy adults whose primary outcome is maximal voluntary strength.
allowed_language: Heavier loading is more specific to a maximal-strength goal.
Experience and technique constrain the starting load.
disallowed_language: Every beginner should start at 80 percent 1RM or above.
The highest-ranked research condition is the best plan for you.
records.limitations: The evidence identifies variables associated with greater group-level strength gains, not a universal first-week dose.

records.statement: Higher weekly resistance-training volume can enhance hypertrophy, with diminishing returns and no justification for assigning a maximizing volume to every beginner.
records.applies_to: Healthy adults training primarily for muscle hypertrophy.
allowed_language: Weekly sets per muscle group are a key hypertrophy dose field.
Volume should progress from a tolerable starting point.
disallowed_language: Ten or more sets per muscle is the required first-week dose for everyone.
More sets always produce proportionally more muscle.
records.limitations: The optimal tradeoff varies with training status, exercise selection, recoverability, and adherence; SportRX lacks individual dose-response validation.

records.statement: Power-oriented resistance training emphasizes intended fast concentric actions and outcome-specific loading rather than simply using the heaviest possible load.
records.applies_to: Healthy adults with a power or physical-performance emphasis and adequate exercise familiarity.
allowed_language: Power training needs a distinct intent and dose from hypertrophy training.
disallowed_language: Heavy lifting alone automatically trains power.
Olympic-style lifts are required for all users.
records.limitations: Exercise complexity, supervision needs, and technical readiness are not determined by this evidence summary.

records.statement: Training to momentary repetition failure is not required for strength or hypertrophy gains and should not be a default instruction across every set and exercise.
allowed_language: Most work sets do not need to end in complete failure.
Effort can be recorded with RIR or RPE alongside actual repetitions and load.
disallowed_language: Every set must reach failure to build muscle.
Non-failure training is ineffective.
records.limitations: Definitions and volume matching vary across studies; this does not establish one exact RIR target for every movement or trainee.

records.statement: RIR is a useful effort-description field but is an estimate, not a measured physiological threshold or proof that a set achieved a precise stimulus.
records.applies_to: Resistance-training sessions where users record repetitions in reserve.
allowed_language: Record estimated RIR to describe how close the set felt to failure.
Review RIR together with load, repetitions, completion, and technique.
disallowed_language: RIR exactly measures muscle activation.
A reported RIR value proves the dose was optimal.
records.limitations: Meta-regression estimates across studies and subjective user reports both contain measurement uncertainty.

records.statement: When weekly hypertrophy volume is equated, training frequency can often be selected to distribute that volume around time, recovery, and preference rather than treated as an isolated magic variable.
records.applies_to: Healthy adults organizing resistance-training volume for hypertrophy.
allowed_language: Frequency can be used to make weekly volume practical and repeatable.
disallowed_language: One exact weekly frequency maximizes hypertrophy for everyone.
records.limitations: The evidence base is heterogeneous and does not remove the need to consider skill practice, per-session fatigue, or individual response.

records.statement: Low-volume resistance training can improve selected 1RM outcomes in resistance-trained men, but this narrow evidence supports a time-constrained option rather than a universal minimum effective dose.
records.applies_to: Resistance-trained men using squat or bench-press focused strength programs under time constraints.
allowed_language: A lower-volume option may still be useful when time is limited.
disallowed_language: One set is the minimum effective dose for every person and exercise.
This evidence applies equally to beginners, women, and every lift.
records.limitations: The review included six studies, trained men, and narrow strength outcomes; the gains were described as suboptimal.

records.statement: Concurrent aerobic and strength training generally does not compromise hypertrophy or maximal-strength development, but same-session organization may matter more for explosive-strength outcomes.
records.applies_to: Healthy adults combining supervised aerobic and resistance training.
allowed_language: Aerobic and resistance training can coexist in one weekly plan.
Session order and separation deserve attention when power is a priority.
disallowed_language: Cardio always kills muscle gain.
Combining modes never creates scheduling tradeoffs.
records.limitations: The review does not prescribe one schedule for every user, and explosive-strength findings should not be generalized to all outcomes.

records.statement: Aerobic exercise produces modest average improvements in body weight, waist circumference, and body-fat measures in adults with overweight or obesity, with larger weekly volumes associated with larger average effects.
records.applies_to: Adults with overweight or obesity in supervised aerobic-training trials lasting at least eight weeks.
allowed_language: Aerobic volume can support body-composition improvement.
Expected average weight change from exercise alone is modest.
disallowed_language: This plan will make you lose a specific number of kilograms.
More exercise guarantees linear weight loss for an individual.
records.limitations: Trial averages cannot predict individual response, and the evidence population is adults with overweight or obesity rather than all SportRX users.

records.statement: A body-composition-oriented exercise plan can combine aerobic and resistance training because the modes contribute different outcomes; exercise mode alone does not define or guarantee weight loss.
records.applies_to: Adults with overweight or obesity seeking exercise support for body-composition goals.
allowed_language: Use aerobic work for energy expenditure and cardiorespiratory benefit while keeping resistance training in the week.
Track training completion separately from body-composition change.
disallowed_language: One exercise mode is universally best for fat loss.
SportRX exercise sessions create a known calorie deficit.
records.limitations: Nutrition, medication, sleep, and clinical care are outside this product pack and substantially affect body-weight outcomes.

records.statement: Resistance exercise during dietary weight loss can help preserve fat-free mass and improve strength, but SportRX must not convert this evidence into nutrition advice or a promised body-composition result.
records.applies_to: Adults aged 18-65 years with overweight or obesity undertaking dietary weight loss in the included evidence.
allowed_language: Resistance training is an important component when preserving muscle is a priority during weight loss.
disallowed_language: This resistance plan guarantees preservation of all lean mass.
SportRX prescribes your diet.
records.limitations: The underlying intervention includes dietary weight loss outside SportRX's present scope and individual responses vary.

records.statement: Exercise adherence varies widely; supervision, combined training, and social support were associated with higher attendance in one obesity-focused review, but no single feature guarantees adherence.
records.applies_to: Adults with obesity in structured exercise interventions.
allowed_language: A plan should be judged partly by whether the user can complete it.
Support and supervision may help some users maintain attendance.
disallowed_language: This interface feature will improve adherence by a known percentage.
Choice alone guarantees that a user will keep training.
records.limitations: The review population and intervention designs were specific and heterogeneous; these are design considerations, not causal product claims.
